subject: Saturn AI — Context & KV-cache impact on dedicated fleet sizing (proposal)
messages:
From: Mina Park <mina@saturn.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Victor Chen <victor@saturn.ai>, procurement@saturn.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing request — 70B model, 64k contexts, expected traffic

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We need a formal sizing estimate for the dedicated pool we discussed so procurement can move the contract forward. High level requirements:
- Model: LLaMA2-70B (we'll want the 64k context variant)
- Typical request size: ~2k prompt tokens, median reply 300 tokens
- Peak QPS target: 200 requests/sec (burst to 400 for short windows)
- Workload pattern: mix of synchronous chat (low-latency) and some async batch scoring; about 70% chat, 30% batch
- Latency SLO for chat: p95 < 600ms

Attached: usage_estimates.csv (token distributions + qps forecasts) and example prompts. Two specific asks:
1) Rough GPU pool size options (constrained by H100-80GB and A100-80GB availability) with and without quantization (FP16 vs int8/4-bit).
2) KV-cache impact for 64k contexts — how much additional GPU memory per request and whether we should recommend prefix/KV offload to host RAM or NVMe.

Can you send an initial ballpark by end of day? We can set up a 60-min sizing call Monday if needed.

Thanks,
Mina Park
VP of Product, Saturn AI
mina@saturn.ai

Attachment stubs: usage_estimates.csv (CSV), example_prompts.json (JSON)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Mina Park <mina@saturn.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — 70B model, 64k contexts, expected traffic

Mina — thanks for the details and the attachments. Putting a concise set of ballpark options below; we'll follow up with a short readout and the slide deck (attached). See kvcache-sim-output.csv for the simulation outputs used to derive these.

Topline (order-of-magnitude):
- FP16 baseline (no quant): LLaMA2-70B weights ~140GB FP16 (order estimate). With 64k context the KV cache can add ~1.1–1.8x the weights footprint depending on implementation and layer hybrids, which means single-GPU serving without sharding is infeasible on 80GB cards. You would need multi-way model sharding across GPUs; for your p95 latency target and 200 QPS, rough pool size is 20–26 x A100/H100-80GB (higher counts for strict p95).

- Int8 or 4-bit quantized path (recommended for production): quantization reduces resident weight memory significantly — practical measured reductions are ~3–4x vs FP16 for production-friendly int8/4-bit kernels. That typically brings the model down into the 35–50GB range (weights in GPU memory), making single-card placement possible on 80GB for the model weights, but KV cache for 64k still occupies substantial memory. With int8 + KV cache optimizations (KV prefix caching + re-use across similar requests) we estimate a dedicated pool of ~5–8 x H100-80GB to meet 200 QPS and p95 < 600ms.

- KV-cache specifics and offload:
  * KV per-token overhead depends on hidden size; for LLaMA2-70B with 64k context we measured KV cache allocations in the range of ~20–50 bytes/token in highly optimized runtimes (varies by key/value precision and compression). That means 64k tokens can add ~1.2–3.2 GB per request in GPU RAM just for KV state in aggressive quantized runtimes, and considerably more in FP16.
  * Recommendation: use hybrid strategy — keep recent prefix segments cached on GPU and offload older segments to host RAM/NVMe with async prefetch for expected chat flows. This reduces the per-request GPU RAM needed while preserving latency for the common case.

Sizing options (ballpark) for your described workload:
- Conservative (no quantization, in-GPU KV): 24 x H100/A100-80GB (multi-GPU sharding + larger pool for tail latency).
- Recommended (int8/4-bit, hybrid KV offload, KV caching heuristics): 6 x H100-80GB + dedicated NVMe-backed KV offload nodes (2x NVMe servers for redundancy).
- Hybrid: start with 3 x H100 for canary (int8 runtime), use autoscaling to 8 x H100 during business hours, NVMe offload enabled.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a canary config that pins the quantized variant and a canary traffic % so you can validate quality/regressions.
- We'll surface cost deltas in the deck: quantized config typically reduces GPU hours by ~60–70% for this workload.

Next steps:
- Internal: Aditya and Lauren — can you review the sim CSV and sanity-check the per-token overhead numbers before EOD?
- External: Mina — I attached the sizing deck (dedicated-sizing-deck.pdf) and kvcache-sim-output.csv. If the numbers look directionally correct, let's schedule Monday 9/20 for a deep-dive.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: kvcache-sim-output.csv (CSV), dedicated-sizing-deck.pdf (PDF)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — quick notes on simulation

Tessa / Lauren — quick pass after checking Mina's CSV and our sim:

- The "20–50 bytes/token" window Tessa called out is aggressive but plausible for int8 KV representations with attention cache compression + block-sparse tricks. For conservative planning use 40 bytes/token as the working number (we used 32 in the attached sim).

- For the 64k context case: at 40 bytes/token that's ~2.56 GB per request of KV on top of weights (for entire context). In practice chat flows reuse large prefixes across requests; if Saturn can accept keeping a 4–8k active GPU-resident prefix (hot window) and offloading the rest, we can cut per-request GPU KV to ~200–400 MB for the most common requests. That is the key lever.

- Alternatives to reduce GPU count for the same SLO:
  * Recommend a split-architecture: latency-sensitive endpoints (chat) served by quantized 33B/34B variants (single-card) and long-context batch/analysis routed to 70B dedicated pool. This avoids sizing the 70B fleet for the full 200 QPS of chat.
  * Another option is model-variant routing: route high-frequency, short-context traffic to a 13–34B model and reserve 70B for complex/long-context sessions.

- Risk/QA: quantization can introduce quality deltas on some prompt types. We should include a 2–4 week QA window in the canary plan with a small labeled prompt set from Saturn (we included a templated evaluation plan in the deck).

I'll polish the sim notes and swap the conservative 40b/token value into the spreadsheet.

-Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — proposed next steps and MAP

Mina / Victor / procurement team — following internal review, here is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and ask list so procurement can move forward: 

1) Shortlist & timeline
   - Week 0: Sign go-ahead for canary (minimal committed capacity).
   - Week 1–2: Provision 3 x H100-80GB nodes (quantized runtime), NVMe offload enabled; run functional validation and quality checks.
   - Week 3–4: Expand to 6 x H100 (production target) if canary passes latency/quality gates.

2) Configs we will deliver
   - Canary config: int8 quantized LLaMA2-70B runtime, hybrid KV offload, autoscaling triggers, monitoring dashboards (token-level cost, p95/p50 latency, KV hit/miss).
   - Production config: recommended 6 x H100-80GB with NVMe offload and 2x NVMe servers for redundancy; fallback routing to 70B sharded pool in region as needed.

3) Procurement ask (to speed contracting)
   - Confirmation on acceptable model variants for canary (do you want us to run quality gate on quantized 70B or pair with a 33B fallback?)
   - Sign-off on shared test prompts and SLA acceptance criteria (we'll provide the evaluation template)

4) Pricing note: the quantized path shows ~60–70% lower GPU-hour spend vs the FP16-sharded alternative in our estimate. We'll include a cost-comparison appendix in the contract addendum.

Next steps: please confirm (a) whether you'd like the 33B fallback enabled in canary and (b) available times for a 60-min sizing/depth call on Monday 9/20. Once confirmed, procurement can attach the updated config to the order form and we can push provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com
